title: Why Hot Water Can Crack a Frozen Windshield
description:
Why can hot water crack a frozen windshield? Glass is slow to move heat. A splash of hot water warms the outer surface and makes it swell in a second, while the glass underneath is still frozen. One side stretches, the other doesn't, and that pull is called thermal shock. If there's already a tiny chip, the stress gathers there and a crack can grow across the glass.

The safe way on an icy morning: never hot water. Use a plastic scraper, a de-icer spray, or start the car and let the defroster warm the glass slowly (not full blast right away).
